components.gap: Only two special cases state a sample space and feasible set: a finite outcome set with normalization only (rationality-4-1) and densities on a bounded interval [A,B] with one mean constraint relative to a stated numerical coordinate (measurement-uncertainty). No general maximum-entropy problem is stated: a sample space with a declared reference measure, finitely many declared constraint functions f_k with prescribed values F_k, and the feasible set of distributions satisfying them (including the possibility that it is empty). Required: state the sample space, the constraint functions and the feasible distributions in general so that the worked distribution solves the declared optimization problem and the coordinate/reference choice remains explicit.

The optimizer is derived with existence/uniqueness only for (i) the finite uniform case and (ii) the bounded-interval single-mean-constraint exponential density. There is no derivation of the optimizer for general declared constraints (the Gibbs/exponential form proportional to exp(-sum_k lambda_k f_k) relative to the reference measure, with optimality proved by the Gibbs inequality), and no existence/uniqueness qualifications for the general case (empty feasible set; constraint values on the boundary of the attainable moment set where the supremum is not attained; unbounded sample spaces where the partition function diverges or entropy is unbounded). Required: derive the optimizer and its existence/uniqueness qualifications under general declared constraints.

evidence.label: annex:p15.measurement.asymmetric-model: Z(lambda), monotone mean, unique lambda

components.gap: Multipliers and normalization are treated only implicitly for one constraint on a bounded interval, where existence of lambda is proved before use. There is no explanation of what the multipliers and the normalizing function Z(lambda_1,...,lambda_m) are in the general method, of the relation F_k = -d log Z / d lambda_k, or of the fact that solving the multiplier equations presupposes that a feasible optimizer exists (with a case where the multiplier equations have no solution or the optimizer is not attained). Required: explain multipliers and normalization without assuming a feasible optimizer exists.

evidence.label: one-sentence statement of the general maximum-entropy proposal; Jaynes named as advocate via the 2003 book

components.gap: The route contains only a one-sentence statement of the maximum-entropy proposal and the name of Jaynes as an advocate. The 1957 normative inferential argument is not reconstructed: entropy as the uncertainty measure singled out by Shannon's conditions; the maximum-entropy assignment as the least biased, maximally noncommittal distribution given the stated expectation information; statistical mechanics recast as statistical inference independent of ergodic or equal a priori hypotheses; and the premises on which the inferential conclusion is conditional (the declared constraints represent all the information used; the chosen enumeration of states/reference measure; the results are best estimates relative to that information, not experimentally guaranteed physical truths). Required: reconstruct the normative inferential argument and its premises so that the inferential interpretation remains conditional on them.

evidence.label: cube factory: side-length vs volume vs face-area uniformity
reference coordinate and constraints are part of the problem
criterion vs bounds; uniform vs maximum-entropy alternative for 16.52

components.gap: The route shows representation dependence of uniformity (cube example), states that the reference coordinate and constraints belong to the entropy problem, and contrasts a uniform model with a mean-constrained maximum-entropy model for the copper coefficient. No example is worked: the maximum-entropy distribution for the changed constraint (mean 16.52 on [16.40,16.92]) is not solved (lambda and the resulting variance are not computed), and no reference-measure example computes how the maximum-entropy solution changes when the reference measure or coordinate changes (e.g., differential entropy under a reparameterization). Required: work a changed-constraint or reference-measure example in which the worked distribution solves the declared optimization problem, separating mathematical optimization from evidential warrant.
